events.title: Global Plates is in Steam Next Fest
events.summary: Global Plates is part of Steam Next Fest, October 19–26. If the fest brought you here, the demo is ready: download it from this page and it goes straight into your library. What you do Build a food factory from conveyors and machines, then open the café and serve a room full of cats. Food goes stale while it waits, so the tightest line wins. Four kitchens (pasta, hamburger, sushi and ramen), about an hour of play. Ten languages The demo is in English, German, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Simplifie

events.title: Demo 1.2: Global Plates now speaks Polish and Spanish!
events.summary: Steam Next Fest runs October 19-26, and the Global Plates demo now speaks two more languages. Polish and Spanish The whole demo is now in Polish and in Spanish - one Spanish written to read naturally in both Spain and Latin America. Menus, the tutorial, the UPGRADES shop, the cafe's OPEN / CLOSED sign and every cat's remarks are translated. The game starts in your Windows language; you can switch any time in Settings > Language. 10 languages English, German, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Simplified

events.title: Demo 1.1 is live for Steam Cooking Fest!

Now in 8 languages English, German, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Turkish. events.title: The demo is out — build a kitchen, open the café, serve the cats
events.summary: The Global Plates demo is live. Press Download Demo on this page and it goes straight into your library. No signup, no key, no waiting. What is in the demo Four levels: the pasta tutorial, Hamburger, Sushi, and Ramen. Ramen unlocks once you have earned enough stars on the café levels. The full café loop. Build your factory in your own time, press START THE DAY, and a timed service day begins. Cats walk in on a schedule with one big rush, sit, eat, react, and pay. Nothing scores and nothing spoil

events.title: Update — the cat café is open: service days, coins, upgrades, and a Sushi level
events.summary: This is the biggest update since the playtest opened. It reworks the core loop around the thing testers asked for most: something to optimise for once a recipe works. The cat café is open Every kitchen now feeds a café. Cats walk in, wait, sit, eat, react, and pay. Build your factory in your own time, then press START THE DAY. A timed service day begins, cats arrive on a schedule with one big rush, and you can keep building while it runs. Nothing scores and nothing spoils while you are planning.

events.title: 2,000 wishlists — thank you
events.summary: Global Plates passed 2,000 wishlists this weekend. A month ago the store page went live with a trailer and five screenshots. Most of you arrived in the last two weeks, and more than a thousand of you are already playing the playtest and telling me what to fix. That is a very different place from where this started. events.title: Hotfix — tutorial highlights, journal clicks, and stalled machines
events.summary: This patch fixes three issues found since the last update. Fixed The tutorial's final step highlighted conveyors pointing toward the wrong place. Clicks on the journal screen passed through to the game behind it. Machines stopped delivering dishes after their output conveyor was deleted. The playtest is free and open — request access from this page. If you play, the feedback survey is the most useful thing you can send. — Fbs Games

events.summary: This update comes from the latest round of playtest feedback. Every change below was requested by a tester. Japanese The game is now fully playable in Japanese. Select it in the settings menu. The Steam store page is also fully available in Japanese. Machines now explain themselves Hovering a machine shows what it does, what it will not accept, and what it produces. events.title: What the first playtest feedback changed
events.summary: The first playtest surveys are in, and a few answers changed my priorities. Thank you to everyone who filled one in. What worked The art, music and overall feel scored highest of anything on the survey. It ran smoothly for every tester, with no bugs reported. And the core loop landed — one player described the best part as getting a level right, then replaying it to build a cleaner, faster layout. That's exactly the game I'm making. events.title: Playtest is LIVE — Request Access now!
events.summary: The kitchen doors are open — our first public Playtest is live! Global Plates is a cozy automation-puzzle game about building conveyor kitchens that cook the world's dishes. Starting today you can play the first slice of it: the Playtest includes the tutorial plus two full levels — discover each recipe, fix the flow, and keep every ingredient fresh on its journey to the plate. How to join Open the Global Plates store page and click Request Access in the Playtest box. We approve testers in waves

events.title: Welcome to Global Plates! 🍝
events.summary: Hi! I'm the solo developer of Global Plates — thanks for stopping by the brand-new store page. Global Plates is a cozy factory-automation journey built around food. Travel a hand-drawn world map, build a new conveyor kitchen in each country, and discover the transformations behind dishes like pizza, sushi, and masala — 9 levels plus a tutorial at launch.
